english.title: Do a prohibited act to a tree in a conservation area - Town and Country Planning Act 1990
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) in a conservation area, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CONSERVATION AREA..), designated by **(..SPECIFY THE AUTHORITY..), did an act, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACT..), which by virtue of section 198(3)(a) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 might have been prohibited by a tree preservation order
english.legislation: Contrary to section 211(1) and 210(1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

english.notes:
Preservation Orders replaced by Preservation Regulations as from 06/04/2012. Therefore this CJS Code and Offence Wording is now OBSOLETE. Now See CJS Code TC90040 and Offence Wording document H~~~~~~~~ .

(i) See H9146 for the either way offence where a tree subject of a tree preservation order is cut down, uprooted, destroyed etc.
(ii) See H9147 for the summary offence where a tree subject of a tree preservation order is otherwise damaged.
(iii) Section 211(3) of the town and Country Planning Act 1990 provides that it shall be a defence for a person charged with an offence under subsection (1) to prove-
(a) that he served notice of his intention to do the act in question (with sufficient particulars to identify the tree) on the local planning authority in whose area the tree is or was situated; and (b) that he did the act in question with the consent of the local planning authority in whose area the tree is or was situated, or after the expiry of the period of six weeks from the date of the notice but before the expiry of the period of two years from that date.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding £20,000.
